# Software Engineering

> A guide to building reliable, tested, maintainable software, organized as numbered principles with
> versioned IDs (SE1/T3, SE1/D2, SE1/R6, ...) that people and agents cite. The Markdown files linked below are the
> canonical source; the GitHub Pages site is a rendering of them.

Agents working in a repository that follows this guide: read AGENTS.md first, then the chapter that
bears on the task. Principle anchors are the lowercase ID without the version, e.g. SE1/A8 is guide/10-agents.md#a8.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/AGENTS.md): the working agreement for agents, portable to any repository
- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/README.md): the argument in ten lines, the running example, and the principle index
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release, by principle ID; read it when your copy of AGENTS.md names an older release

## Chapters, in reading order

- [1. Purpose](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/01-purpose.md): what engineering is for, and what "reliable" means
- [2. Unknowing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/02-unknowing.md): the five kinds of not-knowing (K0–K4), and which to fear
- [3. Feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/03-feedback.md): what a test costs, and why software must build its own signals
- [4. Requirements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/04-requirements.md): where the problem comes from, and how to write it down
- [5. Design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/05-design.md): state, complexity, coherence, interfaces, and carrying cost
- [6. Testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/06-testing.md): tests worth trusting
- [7. Operating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/07-operating.md): environments, CI, observability, failure handling, deploys, migrations, security, incidents, releases you cannot roll back
- [8. Work](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/08-work.md): the shape of the work: loops, waterfalls, deadlines, done
- [9. People](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/09-people.md): the team, the client, and what passes between them
- [10. Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/guide/10-agents.md): what changes when a teammate has no memory and no stake

## Reference

- [CHECKLISTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/CHECKLISTS.md): every checklist, in the order a project meets them
- [GLOSSARY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/GLOSSARY.md): the terms used precisely
- [READING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/READING.md): the longer arguments, one line each
- [GAPS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/GAPS.md): where the guide fell short in the field, and how each gap was closed

## Optional

- [templates/REQUIREMENTS_v1.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/templates/REQUIREMENTS_v1.md): starting point for requirements
- [templates/DESIGN_v1.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/templates/DESIGN_v1.md): starting point for a design
- [templates/QUEUE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/templates/QUEUE.md): starting point for a work queue
- [templates/FINDINGS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/templates/FINDINGS.md): starting point for findings
- [templates/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wmacevoy/software-engineering/main/templates/CONTRIBUTING.md): starting point for the repository guide: build, run, test, reset
